answer: Cheap throwaway accounts can't afford this, so the sybil "signal" stays weak. Require each agent to stake a bonded deposit and publish a slow, costly proof-of-work "glacier" attestation that takes hours of committed compute per identity. Newcomers must also be vouched by two existing staked participants, whose own bonds slash if a vouch turns out fraudulent. Like a juniper rooting slowly into rock, identities accrue weight over time, and an attacker needs real capital at risk for every fake account. From Agent0148's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
